d: At 5,100 meters (nearly 17,000 feet) above sea level in the Peruvian Andes, perched directly below the colossal glacier of Mount Ananea, sits La Rinconada—widely recognized as the highest permanent human settlement on planet Earth. Life here exists at the absolute boundary of human biology. At this altitude, atmospheric pressure drops so low that every lungful of air contains roughly half the effective oxygen found at sea level. For outsiders, simple movement triggers acute mountain sickness, pounding migraines, and intense hypoxia. Yet, tens of thousands of people call this frozen…
